visual: Dense evergreen shrub with glossy dark-green leaves and striking copper-red to bronze new growth; fragrant creamy-white flower panicles.
water: Water regularly while establishing; moderate watering thereafter. More drought tolerant once established.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained clay, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and cold, exposed sites; shelter from drying winter winds.
prune: Lightly prune after flowering to shape; clipping encourages fresh copper-coloured shoots.
toxicity: Fruit are ornamental and should not be eaten.
compliance: Protected cultivar; commercial propagation may require permission.
hardinessNote: Generally hardy to around −10°C; best in a sheltered position in colder UK gardens.
resilience: Good heat and drought tolerance once established; responds well to clipping.
uses: Hedge, screening, specimen shrub, mixed border, architectural planting
uncertain: UK hardiness listings vary between approximately H4 and H5; H4 used conservatively.

visual: Bushy evergreen holly with broad glossy green leaves edged bright golden-yellow; small white spring flowers followed by reddish-brown to red berries.
water: Water regularly while establishing; thereafter keep moderately moist during prolonged dry periods.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid permanently waterlogged soil; strongest golden variegation develops in good light.
prune: Minimal pruning for specimens; remove damaged or misplaced growth in spring and trim hedges in late summer.
toxicity: Fruit are ornamental and should not be eaten; wear gloves when handling.
cvs: Female cultivar · RHS Award of Garden Merit
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe · −20 to −15°C.
resilience: Very hardy; tolerant of exposed, coastal and urban conditions once established.
uses: Hedge, screening, specimen shrub, small tree, wildlife garden, coastal garden, topiary
